To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose a new experience-based motion planner that is able to solve high-dimensional problems in varying environments with variable obstacles, 2) we show that the planner can reduce planning time and memory requirements by an order of magnitude when compared to the state-of-the-art, 3) our planner is able to solve problems with 10,000 times as many configurations as the state-of-the art, 4) we show that our approach is able to learn from past experiences in varying environments

We present an experience based planning framework that uses a graph to store past experiences and that is on average an orders of magnitude faster than an existing approach that uses individual paths.

experience-based planning using a SPARS representation is more efficient than using individual paths for storing past experiences, and that experience-based planning is more efficient than planning from scratch in high dimensional configuration spaces.
